newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges IRA to respond to new ceasefire appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges IRA to respond to new ceasefire appeal.

text.p: The United States welcomed on Friday an appeal by the Irish Republican Army's's political wing, Sinn Fein, for the republican guerrillas to renew their truce in Northern Ireland.

"We welcome the news that the Sinn Fein leadership has urged the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, to call a new ceasefire. And we ... urge the Irish Republican Army to implement a lasting ceasefire," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams earlier urged the IRA to call a new truce in their 28-year-old war against British rule in Northern Ireland. Such a move would pave the way for Sinn Fein to enter all-party peace talks on the British province.
Adams said he would not have asked the outlawed guerrilla group to call a new truce if he had not been confident of a positive response.

President Bill Clinton has been active in trying to get peace talks going and Burns noted that Washington had said it would not support the inclusion of Sinn Fein unless an effective IRA ceasefire was in place.
